note: Whether each surveyed bird stays where it breeds, DECLARED from North Ground's own published species profile and quoted verbatim (statedAs, from the named profile field); src/lib/hunt/intelligence/seasonal-truth.test.ts checks every quote against the published text. It decides which season a breeding-survey surface can speak for: RESIDENT and SHORT_DISTANCE birds live in the autumn where they breed, so their June survey stands all year; PARTIAL, MIGRATORY and UNDECLARED birds are read as breeding-season evidence only, and a hunting-season surface drawn from September-to-February records speaks for the hunting months. UNDECLARED is the reading that claims least, used where the published profile says nothing about movement.

classes.RESIDENT: Does not migrate: where it breeds is where it lives in the hunting season.
classes.SHORT_DISTANCE: Moves locally or up and down slope: its hunting-season range broadly follows where it breeds.
classes.PARTIAL: Some populations stay and others leave: the breeding pattern holds only where birds stay.
classes.MIGRATORY: Breeds in one place and spends the hunting season in another.
classes.UNDECLARED: The published profile does not say; read as moving, which claims least.

species:american-black-duck.statedAs: northern breeders migrate far, coastal birds only short distances

species:american-coot.statedAs: Some populations are resident, others migrate

species:american-crow.statedAs: Resident in many areas; birds breeding north of southern Canada move south for winter

species:american-wigeon.statedAs: winters from southern Alaska and the Pacific Northwest across much of the southern and coastal United States into Mexico and Central America

species:american-woodcock.statedAs: many move south ahead of major fall cold fronts

species:band-tailed-pigeon.statedAs: Present year-round in parts of the Pacific Coast; mainly a summer resident elsewhere.

species:barrows-goldeneye.statedAs: Winters mainly on shallow, protected coastal bays and estuaries

species:black-bellied-whistling-duck.statedAs: not strongly migratory, and flocks disappear from some northern breeding areas in winter

species:black-billed-magpie.statedAs: Mostly a permanent resident, with some upslope movement in fall and a few moving south or downslope in winter

species:blue-winged-teal.statedAs: Winters from the southern U.S. to South America

species:brewers-blackbird.statedAs: present year-round in parts of the western U.S. and winters east to the southeastern U.S. and Mexico

species:brown-headed-cowbird.statedAs: winters from the northern U.S. south

species:bufflehead.statedAs: breeds in northern forests and winters farther south and on the coasts

species:canada-goose.statedAs: some populations migrate while others remain resident

species:canvasback.statedAs: winters on the Great Lakes, Pacific coast and mid-Atlantic coast

species:chukar.statedAs: Permanent resident in its North American range

species:cinnamon-teal.why: The published profile says nothing about whether this bird moves between seasons. Read as moving, the reading that claims least, until a sourced statement is added.

species:clapper-rail.statedAs: Found year-round in many parts of its range; some withdrawal from the northern Atlantic end in winter

species:common-goldeneye.statedAs: south in winter to California, Texas, the Southeast and Florida

species:common-grackle.statedAs: winters from Kansas, the southern Great Lakes and New England south

species:common-merganser.statedAs: Migrates late in fall and early in spring

species:common-raven.statedAs: Mostly a permanent resident; some wander in fall and winter south of the breeding range

species:dusky-grouse.statedAs: Unusual uphill altitudinal migration: moves up into dense conifer forest in autumn, up to about 30 miles.

species:european-starling.statedAs: Northern birds mostly move south in fall, migrating by day; southern birds may be permanent residents

species:fish-crow.statedAs: Mostly a permanent resident; withdraws from some inland parts of its range in winter.

species:fulvous-whistling-duck.statedAs: Regular migration by some Gulf Coast birds to southern Mexico, overshadowed by widespread wandering

species:gadwall.statedAs: Migrates in flocks but is not a long-distance migrant

species:gambels-quail.why: The published profile says nothing about whether this bird moves between seasons. Read as moving, the reading that claims least, until a sourced statement is added.

species:great-tailed-grackle.statedAs: Resident from southeastern California and southern Nevada east to southern Nebraska and southwestern Missouri

species:greater-prairie-chicken.statedAs: Some birds are permanent residents; others move up to about 160 km (100 miles) between breeding and wintering areas.

species:greater-sage-grouse.statedAs: Largely non-migratory, with local movements out of high valleys in winter.

species:greater-scaup.statedAs: Breeds in Alaska and northern Canada and winters along both the Pacific and Atlantic coasts

species:green-winged-teal.statedAs: Main fall migration is late, mostly October to early December

species:hooded-merganser.statedAs: winters mainly along the Pacific, Atlantic and Gulf slopes

species:lesser-scaup.statedAs: winters from southern British Columbia and the southern Great Lakes and New England south through the southern U.S. to Central America

species:mallard.statedAs: winters in southern Ontario and British Columbia and farther south

species:mottled-duck.statedAs: Mostly non-migratory; makes local movements as habitat conditions change

species:mountain-quail.statedAs: High-elevation birds migrate downslope on foot for winter

species:mourning-dove.statedAs: Some remain through winter across most of the breeding range while northern birds move south.

species:mute-swan.statedAs: North American birds move only as far as needed

species:northern-pintail.statedAs: breeding in the North and wintering to the south

species:northern-shoveler.statedAs: winters across the southern United States and coasts

species:red-breasted-merganser.statedAs: winters mainly on coastal waters of the United States and southern Canada

species:red-winged-blackbird.statedAs: migrates in flocks and is present year-round in many areas

species:redhead.statedAs: winters across the southern United States

species:ring-necked-duck.statedAs: winters from the southwestern and southeastern U.S. south to Central America

species:ruddy-duck.statedAs: northern breeders winter south to Central America

species:ruffed-grouse.statedAs: Permanent resident, but may shift short distances to denser cover for winter.

species:sandhill-crane.statedAs: Northern populations migrate long distances in flocks and formations; Florida, Mississippi and Cuban populations are resident.

species:scaled-quail.statedAs: Permanent resident of the arid southwestern United States

species:sharp-tailed-grouse.statedAs: Resident locally from Alaska and Yukon east to western Quebec

species:sooty-grouse.statedAs: Resident from coastal southeastern Alaska and coastal British Columbia

species:sora.statedAs: migrates mostly at night, many to South America

species:virginia-rail.statedAs: Most migrate to the southern United States and northern Mexico

species:wild-turkey.statedAs: Not migratory, but may wander, especially in fall.

species:willow-ptarmigan.statedAs: Less migratory than rock ptarmigan but sometimes winters south of the breeding range

species:wilsons-snipe.statedAs: winters commonly across the southern United States

species:wood-duck.statedAs: northern birds migrate while southern females may be resident.

species:yellow-headed-blackbird.statedAs: winters from central California, Arizona and Texas south into Mexico
